correctness.rationale: For Aη from source, exact Cayley-Hamilton Aη²=−(1−2η²)I. Determinant-one exponential and its Frobenius square 2+4h² sin²(kτ)/k² give all singular values and the gain. Derivative monotonicity on first positive lobe, followed by strict damping over later lobes, gives the unique global maximum for 0<r<h and G=1 otherwise. Direct substitution r=sk produces the nonconstant profile and limiting peak-time law, including exact EP endpoint. A standalone standard-library checker compared independent 2x2 matrix singular norms, the gain, peak time and crossover at thousands of points; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: A natural quantitative gap in the motivating nonreciprocal dynamics: known asymptotic eigenvalue stability and numerical-abscissa onset do not specify largest possible perturbation burst or when it occurs. The theorem supplies a full all-parameter sharp gain and time, and an analytically nonconstant exceptional-point crossover profile distinguishing damping/frequency paths. Its limiting profile has interpretable weak-damping and Jordan-block ends. This is stronger than a textbook eigenvalue calculation and addresses the source’s physically motivated transient regime.
